description: Unique identifier for each river monitoring site
New Zealand regional council the site belongs to
Name of the river catchment the monitoring site drains
Latitude of the monitoring site in decimal degrees
Longitude of the monitoring site in decimal degrees
Dominant land cover class of the catchment from the Watershed Framework Survey. Categories: Rural, Forest, Urban
Altitude class of the catchment from the Watershed Framework Survey. Categories: lowland, upland
Catchment land cover type from the River Environment Classification. Categories: Pasture, Native vegetation, Exotic forest, Urban
Mean annual rainfall at the site location in millimetres averaged over the period 1970 to 2000. Higher values indicate wetter catchments
Percentage of the upstream catchment used for cropland
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by all forest types combined including both native and exotic forest
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by grassland and other herbaceous vegetation
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by scrub and shrubland
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by urban areas, bare surfaces, or lightly vegetated land
Percentage of the upstream catchment used for cropping and horticulture
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by exotic or plantation forest such as pine
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by exotic grassland, which is the primary indicator of pastoral farming land use. Higher values indicate more intensive agricultural land use
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by exotic scrub and shrubland
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by indigenous or native forest. Higher values generally indicate less disturbed catchments with lower contamination pressure
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by indigenous scrub and shrubland
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by tussock grassland, typically found in upland and high country areas
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by urban area. Higher values indicate greater urban land use pressure
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by other herbaceous vegetation types
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by natural bare or lightly vegetated surfaces such as riverbeds, rock, and alpine areas
Percentage of the upstream catchment covered by artificial bare surfaces including roads, car parks, and mines

Median E. coli concentration at the monitoring site in MPN per 100mL. E. coli is a bacterium indicating faecal contamination. Higher values indicate greater contamination and poorer water quality. This is the primary regression target.

Median dissolved reactive phosphorus concentration in mg per litre. Phosphorus enters waterways primarily through agricultural runoff and is a key driver of algal growth. Higher values indicate greater phosphorus contamination
Median water clarity measured as Secchi depth in metres. Higher values indicate clearer water. Lower values indicate greater sediment or algal contamination

Median ammoniacal nitrogen concentration in mg per litre. Elevated levels can be toxic to aquatic life and indicate inputs from agricultural or wastewater sources. Higher values indicate poorer water quality
Median nitrate nitrogen concentration measured as NO3-N in mg per litre. Nitrate is a key nutrient derived from fertiliser and animal waste. Higher values indicate more intensive land use pressure
Median total oxidised nitrogen concentration in mg per litre representing the combined oxidised nitrogen forms in the water. Higher values indicate greater nitrogen contamination

NPS-FM 2020 attribute band for E. coli assigned based on the long-term median concentration. A = below 130 MPN per 100mL (best), B = 130 to 260 MPN per 100mL, C = 260 to 540 MPN per 100mL, D = 540 to 1000 MPN per 100mL, E = above 1000 MPN per 100mL (worst). This is the primary classification target.

NPS-FM 2020 attribute band for dissolved reactive phosphorus based on annual median concentration. A = below 0.006 mg per litre (best), B = 0.006 to 0.015 mg per litre, C = 0.015 to 0.054 mg per litre, D = above 0.054 mg per litre (worst)

NPS-FM 2020 attribute band for nitrate nitrogen based on annual median concentration. A = below 0.11 mg per litre (best), B = 0.11 to 0.58 mg per litre, C = 0.58 to 1.66 mg per litre, D = above 1.66 mg per litre (worst)

NPS-FM 2020 attribute band for water clarity measured as Secchi depth. Bands run from A (best, clearest water) through B, C to D (worst, least clear). Thresholds vary by river sediment class as defined in NPS-FM 2020

NPS-FM 2020 attribute band for ammoniacal nitrogen. Bands run from A (best, lowest levels) through B to C (worst, highest levels). Thresholds are pH adjusted and vary by river conditions as defined in NPS-FM 2020

NPS-FM 2020 attribute band for total oxidised nitrogen, used as a proxy for nitrate at sites where nitrate is not directly measured. A = below 0.11 mg per litre (best), B = 0.11 to 0.58 mg per litre, C = 0.58 to 1.66 mg per litre, D = above 1.66 mg per litre (worst)
NPS-FM 2020 attribute band for total oxidised nitrogen. A = below 0.11 mg per litre (best), B = 0.11 to 0.58 mg per litre, C = 0.58 to 1.66 mg per litre, D = above 1.66 mg per litre (worst)
